source: TBPN — Anthropic S-1, GPU prices, SpaceX, AI agents; infrastructure/bio/energy outlook
summary: GPU cluster operational execution is a major differentiator — only a handful of operators can reliably energize and run large clusters
summary_extended: Baker argues that successfully standing up and operating large GPU clusters is extraordinarily difficult — analogous to running a Formula 1 team — and that only a small number of operators have demonstrated the competence to do it reliably. He specifically names CoreWeave, Crusoe, Nebius, SpaceX, and the major hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) as proven operators, while suggesting that the many new entrants who have secured land, power, and off-take agreements will fail to energize GPUs on time. This operational failure among inexperienced operators will effectively concentrate GPU compute supply with the competent few, giving them pricing power and market share. The investment implication is to favor the proven operators — particularly the publicly listed ones like CoreWeave — over unproven entrants, as supply concentration benefits those who can actually execute at scale.
